original_question: For a one-dimensional Pisot inflation tiling with scaling factor λ, must the coincidence rank divide the algebraic norm of λ? Here the coincidence rank is the almost-everywhere multiplicity of the factor map from the tiling dynamical system to its maximal equicontinuous factor.
correct_elements: Your draft already tracks the paper’s displayed conjecture very closely. It has the correct scope (one-dimensional Pisot inflation tilings), the correct invariant (coincidence rank), the correct divisibility claim (division by the algebraic norm of λ), and it reproduces the paper’s immediate definition of coincidence rank as the almost-everywhere multiplicity of the factor map to the maximal equicontinuous factor.
missing_details: A stand-alone version should define what “Pisot” means here: λ is a real algebraic integer greater than 1 whose algebraic conjugates all have modulus less than 1.

It should identify the ambient number field for the norm, namely Q(λ), and spell out that the algebraic norm is N_{Q(λ)/Q}(λ), an integer; divisibility is in Z, equivalently by its absolute value if one wants to avoid sign ambiguity.
The universal quantifier should be explicit: the conjecture asks whether this holds for every one-dimensional Pisot inflation tiling.
The coincidence rank should be explicitly attached to the factor map of the associated tiling dynamical system, not just mentioned abstractly.

For paper-faithfulness, it is worth noting that Conjecture 2.2.3 is presented as the non-unimodular extension of the preceding Homological Pisot Conjecture, but the displayed statement itself does not add any extra cohomological hypothesis.
refined_question: Let T be a one-dimensional Pisot inflation tiling with scaling factor λ, where λ > 1 is a real algebraic integer all of whose Galois conjugates have modulus less than 1. If cr(T) denotes the almost-everywhere multiplicity of the factor map from the tiling dynamical system of T to its maximal equicontinuous factor, must cr(T) divide the algebraic norm N_{Q(λ)/Q}(λ) of λ (equivalently, its absolute value)?
justification: The draft is targeting the Coincidence Rank Conjecture stated in Section 2.2, not the broader Pisot Substitution Conjecture or the preceding Homological Pisot Conjecture. Conjecture 2.2.3 is the nearest official formulation, and the next sentence in the paper supplies exactly the definition of coincidence rank used in your draft. The only substantive refinements needed to make the question fully stand-alone are to define the Pisot condition on λ, make the number-field norm explicit, and state the universal quantifier plainly. I have not added any cohomological hypothesis, because Conjecture 2.2.3 as displayed in this paper does not state one, even though the surrounding sentence presents it as an extension of Conjecture 2.2.2.
